expected.literal_gap: Literally, “plans exist on Saturday”; in use, “I have plans on Saturday.” The person with the plans is understood from context, not stated in Korean.

items.input: I will be busy next week

expected.natural_english: I will be busy next week
expected.literal_gap: The default reading here is “will be busy next week.” Depending on subject and context, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 can also express a prediction or probability, such as “probably busy.”
Literally, “rain comes now”; in use, “it is raining right now.” Korean uses rain as the subject rather than a dummy “it.”

expected.literal_gap: Literally, “I saw the test well”; in use, “I did well on the test.” 시험을 보다 means to take an exam, not look at one.
